proposal.summary: Most of this layer keeps its current picks on verified merit, not incumbency: NautilusTrader's engine pin, alpaca-py, and LEAN-as-oracle all reconfirm current/maintained/no-drift on 2026-09-26 primary sources. Reading current main (not just the frozen 2026-09-22 adjudication) resolves one open_gap and sharpens the other. (1) adaptive-paper-alpaca-adapter (c5) now earns_it: it passed a real native paper-broker trial on 2026-09-23 (5 orders, 4 fills, cash-reconciled) that did not exist at adjudication time, and it is the *only* Alpaca path into Nautilus, since NautilusTrader carries zero upstream Alpaca code (RFC nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#3374 open since 2026-01-01, PR #3375 closed unmerged same day). (2) nautilus-ibkr-adapter (c7) is genuinely challenged: I independently confirmed via `gh api` (2026-09-26) that github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#4983 is still open, and its own title states the pinned v2.0.0rc5 Rust adapter's "execution client venue `IB` never matches instrument venue `SMART`, so every stock order is denied locally" -- a verified, currently-unpatched defect, not merely an untested boundary. The one visible fix candidate, PR #5041, is open/unmerged/"dirty" as of today. Meanwhile this repo's own receipt-20260923-passed.json shows the same project's older, non-pinned NautilusTrader 1.231.0 Python IBKR adapter already completing a real paper-Gateway accept/cancel/fill/flatten cycle with a reconciled-flat proof -- a zero-new-dependency interim path. Going beyond the given candidate list, per today's own alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926 artifact plus my direct gh api/PyPI checks: ml4t/backtest+data+live (MIT, pushed within the last 1-2 days, built-in LEAN-parity preset, same author lineage as this catalog's zipline-reloaded) is a fresher, better-licensed comparison-engine candidate than the already-catalogued Lumibot (GPL-3.0, reconfirmed) or StrateQueue (AGPL-3.0), worth a bounded parity trial using the existing frozen SPY fixture. Independently reconfirmed via `gh api`: LEAN's 17-commit drift beyond its pin is not capability-neutral as earlier framed -- it added combo orders (#9822) and OCO/OTO/OUO/bracket contingent orders (#9828, tests #9833) to LEAN's own Alpaca brokerage model.

winner_status.note: Engine pin verified still-current 2026-09-26 via my own gh api check: v2.0.0rc5 remains the top GitHub release (prerelease=true, no rc6/GA), matching https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/releases/tag/v2.0.0rc5. Native synthetic execution evidence (evidence/receipts/native-nautilus-v2-20260920.json, local checkout) is unchanged. This status covers the engine choice itself; its bundled IBKR execution boundary is tracked separately below as challenged, since engine currency does not extend to that specific adapter's correctness.

Pin v0.44.0 still latest on GitHub+PyPI, zero drift. Both 2026-09-22 adjudication lanes already agreed on this component (evidence/artifacts/layer-verdicts-20260922/adjudication/us-equities-execution-broker-20260922.json, local checkout, read directly: 'A and B agree on c4 (alpaca-py)'). Native execution evidence (blueprints/us-equities/paper-e2e-20260921/paper-receipt.json, local checkout: write_attempts 2, cash_delta_usd -0.08, positions 0) unaffected by any new finding.

Retained comparison oracle only, not a live destination (catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json, local checkout, disposition 'selected' for that role; evidence_kind native_execution via blueprints/us-equities/historical-simulation/receipt.json). New finding, independently reconfirmed via `gh api repos/QuantConnect/Lean/commits` on 2026-09-26: the pin's 17-commit drift is not capability-neutral as earlier framed -- it includes 'feature: support combo orders in the alpaca brokerage model' (#9822, 2026-09-23) and 'Add contingent orders: OCO, OTO, OUO and brackets' (#9828, 2026-09-25) with matching tests (#9833). This doesn't change the oracle role, but the pin (985ef30a) is now missing real order-type capability upstream in LEAN's own Alpaca brokerage adapter -- worth a pin refresh before that adapter is used for anything beyond pure SPY/LEAN parity.

This is c5 from the split 2-2 adjudication; both lanes already kept it, but at that time (evidence/artifacts/layer-verdicts-20260922/.../adjudication json, local checkout) its own broker evidence was 'not_started' / 0 broker_connections. Reading current main closes that gap: blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper/receipt.json (local checkout) records trial adaptive-20260923g, source_commit 843dc8f -- which I confirmed is a real commit in this checkout's git log ('Fix three engine defects exposed by live SIP paper trials...#123') -- with orders_submitted 5, cancels 1, native_fill_events 4, two completed round-trips (INTC, GOOGL), and reconciliation cash_delta_usd -0.28 with cash_match true / positions_match true / open_orders 0. This is dated native_execution evidence from 2026-09-23. It is also the only Alpaca path into NautilusTrader: NautilusTrader carries zero upstream Alpaca adapter code (RFC nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#3374 open since 2026-01-01, PR #3375 closed unmerged the same day, per evidence/artifacts/alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926/landscape.json's facts_check section, local checkout, dated 2026-09-26).

This is c7, the other half of the split 2-2 adjudication. Sharper primary-source finding, independently confirmed via `gh api` on 2026-09-26: github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4983 is still OPEN (last updated 2026-09-12, so unworked for two weeks), and its own title states the defect directly -- 'execution client venue `IB` never matches instrument venue `SMART`, so every stock order is denied locally' -- on the exact pinned v2.0.0rc5 Rust adapter this layer needs for US-equity IBKR execution. This is stronger than the prior 'not yet run' framing in evidence/receipts/native-nautilus-v2-20260920.json and catalogs/us-equities/runtime-target.json's broker_boundaries.ibkr block (local checkout): it is a verified, currently-unpatched defect, not just an untested boundary. The one visible upstream work here, PR #5041 ('Refactor Interactive Brokers adapter and add execution client order identity hooks'), is open, unmerged, and shows mergeable_state 'dirty' as of 2026-09-26 (gh api pulls/5041); it touches the same adapter's connection/enums/symbology files (gh api pulls/5041/files) but is not confirmed to close #4983 and should not be assumed to. A verified-working alternative already exists in this project's own history with zero new dependency: blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/ibkr-paper-orders/evidence/receipt-20260923-passed.json (local checkout) shows the same project's older, non-pinned NautilusTrader 1.231.0 Python IBKR adapter completing accept-resting/cancel/fill/flatten against a real paper IB Gateway (port 4002) with an independent official-ibapi flat-proof (0 positions, 0 open orders). The managed-gateway dependency itself, gnzsnz/ib-gateway-docker, is unaffected -- the #4983 defect lives in Nautilus's own Rust execution-client code, not the container. Status is 'challenged' rather than 'unverified' because the incumbent pinned path's failure mode is now verified, not merely unproven.

challengers.name: NautilusTrader 1.231.0 Python IBKR adapter (in-project dual-track/rollback, same upstream)
challengers.why_better: Already has a passed native-paper IBKR execution receipt in this repo (accept/cancel/fill/flatten, real commissions, reconciled-flat proof) while the currently pinned v2.0.0rc5 Rust adapter has a confirmed-open blocking defect (nautechsystems/nautilus_trader#4983, verified open on 2026-09-26) that denies every stock order locally, with no merged fix (PR #5041 open/unmerged/'dirty' as of 2026-09-26).
challengers.trial_plan: Rerun the existing, already-committed blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/ibkr-paper-orders harness (run.py/plan.json, same repo, no new install) unchanged against the pinned v2.0.0rc5 Rust adapter first, to reconfirm the #4983 denial is still live today. Pass criterion for keeping 1.231.0 as the qualified interim IBKR path: rc5 reproduces the denial while 1.231.0 continues to pass the identical accept/cancel/fill/flatten/reconcile contract it already passed on 2026-09-23 (receipt-20260923-passed.json). Overturn condition: rc5 (or a later tag) passes this same fixture once #4983 is closed by a merged fix -- at that point re-pin to rc5/GA and retire the 1.231.0 dual-track.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: paper acts passed / paper fills for the IBKR broker boundary specifically -- currently the layer's only fully-blocked broker boundary; unblocks it using an existing in-repo fixture and an already-qualified older pin, zero new installs.
sources: https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/pull/5041 (open, unmerged, mergeable_state=dirty, checked via gh api 2026-09-26)

challengers.name: ml4t (ml4t-backtest + ml4t-data + ml4t-live)
challengers.why_better: MIT across all three packages (cleaner license fit than Lumibot's confirmed GPL-3.0 or StrateQueue's AGPL-3.0), verified actively maintained within the last 1-2 days as of this check (ml4t/backtest pushed 2026-09-24 with a same-day v0.1.12 release, 28 stars; ml4t/data pushed 2026-09-25, 50 stars; ml4t/live pushed 2026-09-24, 22 stars, latest commit 'Make Live workflows and book links verifiable #106'), and ships a purpose-built LEAN-parity preset plus its own shadow-to-paper-to-live broker runtime (ml4t/live) -- a closer match to this layer's own preregistered SPY/LEAN-parity and broker-boundary requirements than the more generic Lumibot/StrateQueue wrappers already in the catalog. Same author lineage (ml4trading.io) as this catalog's already-accepted zipline-reloaded.
challengers.trial_plan: Run the existing frozen SPY 'one_zero' parity fixture through ml4t-backtest's own 'lean' preset via the already-in-repo blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus/spy-parity/compare.py, exactly as already proposed in evidence/artifacts/alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926/README.md's 'Recommended next steps' (local checkout, dated 2026-09-26). Pass criterion: same preregistered parity tolerance already used for the Nautilus/LEAN comparison. Only after a pass would a single Alpaca paper round trip ever run, under the existing alpaca-paper-smoke contract with one owned writer. Overturn condition: fails preregistered parity tolerance, or pre-1.0 API instability (0.1.x, 44 PyPI releases in under a year) breaks the frozen fixture -- then it stays reference-only.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none yet -- this is a second independent comparison/oracle candidate, not a proposed execution destination; no paper-lane number moves until/unless a parity pass promotes it further.

rejected.name: Lumibot

rejected.reason: license and metadata only -- AGPL-3.0 (stronger copyleft than Lumibot), PyPI release lagging ~13 months behind source HEAD, 214 stars; a deployment shim wrapping an existing strategy, not a demonstrated execution-boundary advantage.

rejected.reason: off-requirement -- wraps the same alpaca-py calls this project already owns as a single writer; adds an agent-facing order-entry surface, not a new execution capability, and would need its own duplicate-writer ownership guard before any use.

rejected.reason: off-requirement (same agent-surface reasoning as alpaca-mcp-server), plus borderline unmaintained -- last commit 2025-10-23, about 11 months old as of 2026-09-26; worth rechecking soon.

rejected.name: ThetaGang
rejected.reason: off-requirement -- an options-wheel strategy bot, not reusable for this project's equity-extreme-mover focus; valuable only as an implementation-pattern reference, not a component to adopt.

rejected.name: tastytrade (tastyware SDK)
rejected.reason: off-requirement -- this project's broker scope is explicitly Alpaca + IBKR only; zero presence in this project's catalog or receipts today. A discovery note for a possible future third broker, not a current adoption case.

rejected.name: schwab-py
rejected.reason: unmaintained -- main branch HEAD and the last tagged release are both over 13 months old; the repo's recent-looking pushed_at metadata lands on side/patch branches, not main. Also off-requirement, since Schwab is outside current project scope.

rejected.name: Clear Street API
rejected.reason: off-requirement -- requires opening and funding a real institutional brokerage account plus an options-suitability questionnaire, which contradicts this project's paper-lane-only research scope and this task's own no-live-account/no-order constraint. Not an installable OSS SDK, so it cannot be evaluated further without opening an account.

rejected.name: QuantRocket
rejected.reason: off-requirement -- surfaced in evidence/artifacts/alpaca-platform-landscape-20260926 (local checkout, 2026-09-26). Its paper-trading route requires first validating a real live account, which this project's explicit paper-lane-only policy forbids; also proprietary/commercial and self-hosted, not an OSS SDK comparison.

researched_candidates.name: NautilusTrader
researched_candidates.fit: Already the selected destination; upstream check confirms the pin is current with zero drift. The IBKR adapter's own docs (read directly at the pin) claim full execution capability, but this is a source_review claim -- the project's own receipt (native-nautilus-v2-20260920.json) still records 'No IBKR Gateway/TWS authentication, data entitlement, adapter connectivity', so the IBKR execution boundary itself remains not_established, unchanged since the pin. 29,418 stars and a push today make it the most actively maintained engine in this set.

researched_candidates.name: alpaca-py
researched_candidates.fit: Already the selected official Alpaca SDK; confirmed current with no upstream drift or notable interface change since the pin. The project's own paper-e2e receipt (one reconciled long-to-flat SPY roundtrip) is unaffected by this check. 1,532 stars, Apache-2.0, actively maintained.

researched_candidates.name: LEAN (QuantConnect)
researched_candidates.fit: Retained oracle only; this check found no capability change since the pin, just routine upstream drift. 21,787 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed daily -- clearly maintained, just not release-tagged in the GitHub sense.

researched_candidates.name: ib_async
researched_candidates.fit: Strongest maintained community alternative to the archived ib_insync for any code path needing a Python-native IBKR client outside Nautilus's own bundled adapter. 1,745 stars, BSD-2-Clause. No local broker/recovery comparison in this stack shows a need to switch from Nautilus's adapter.

researched_candidates.name: ib_insync
researched_candidates.fit: Confirmed dead upstream -- do not adopt. Historical reference only; kept in this list solely to document what ib_async replaced, matching the awesome-list notes' own flag.

researched_candidates.name: ibapi (official Interactive Brokers TWS API, Python client)
researched_candidates.fit: Relevant as ground truth for IBKR wire-protocol behavior, but nobody should depend on the PyPI mirror directly given the multi-year staleness; Nautilus's own adapter and ib_async are the practical current interfaces built on top of it.

researched_candidates.name: Lumibot
researched_candidates.fit: The strongest broker-agnostic strategy-execution alternative to a bespoke per-broker adapter found in this search. Still needs the same data/risk/order-recovery/accounting comparison the layer's overturn_when clause requires before it could replace the selected NautilusTrader destination, and its GPL-3.0 license needs an explicit fit check against the rest of the stack's licenses before any adoption.

researched_candidates.name: StrateQueue
researched_candidates.fit: A lighter-weight deployment shim than Lumibot for wrapping an existing strategy. The PyPI release lag and much smaller community make it a secondary option, not a leading alternative to the selected destination.

researched_candidates.name: alpaca-mcp-server
researched_candidates.fit: Relevant only if an LLM-agent-driven order-entry surface is wanted on top of the existing Alpaca account. It wraps the same alpaca-py calls the project already owns as a single writer, so it adds an agent-facing interface rather than a new execution capability, and would need its own ownership/duplicate-writer guard before use.

researched_candidates.name: IB_MCP
researched_candidates.fit: The only IBKR-side MCP found; relevant if an agent-facing IBKR order-entry surface is wanted to mirror alpaca-mcp-server, but its ~11-month commit gap versus alpaca-mcp-server's days-old cadence, and its much smaller community, are real maintenance-risk signals to re-check before adoption -- borderline on the unmaintained flag and worth rechecking in a few months.

researched_candidates.name: ib-gateway-docker (gnzsnz)
researched_candidates.fit: Not a broker SDK itself but the infrastructure every IBKR execution path in this stack (Nautilus's optional DockerizedIBGateway, or any ib_async script) depends on to run headless. Already named in the project's own landscape catalog as a 'Dockerized IB Gateway' candidate; independently confirmed here as current and as the exact dependency Nautilus's own docs point to.

researched_candidates.name: ThetaGang
researched_candidates.fit: Not directly reusable (options wheel strategy, not the equity-extreme-mover focus), but the strongest concrete, currently-maintained reference found for what a real-money IBKR execution loop looks like end-to-end -- a useful implementation-pattern check against this project's own unqualified nautilus-ibkr-adapter path.

researched_candidates.name: tastytrade (tastyware/tastytrade)
researched_candidates.fit: New find beyond the given star/awesome-list inputs. Tastytrade is a modern, API-friendly US options/equities broker with a much faster-moving community SDK than either ib_async or schwab-py checked here; worth tracking as a lower-friction third broker option if the IBKR adapter's not_established broker acceptance or Alpaca's scope ever becomes a blocker -- but it has zero presence in this project's own catalog or receipts today, so this is a discovery note, not a recommendation to adopt.

researched_candidates.name: schwab-py
researched_candidates.fit: New find beyond the given lists, nominally the successor ecosystem to the dead tda-api, but flag UNMAINTAINED by this task's 12-month rule despite an active-looking repository page -- the apparent August 2026 activity is confined to non-main branches. Not in this project's current scope (Alpaca + IBKR only); if Schwab is ever considered, re-verify freshness before relying on this specific wrapper.

researched_candidates.name: Clear Street API
researched_candidates.fit: An institutional-grade alternative broker beyond the retail-focused Alpaca/IBKR/Schwab/Tastytrade set, with reference data and corporate events in the same surface as execution. Interesting for a later production-scale destination, but it is a commercial account relationship rather than an installable OSS SDK, so it cannot be evaluated further without opening an account -- out of scope for this read-only research pass.
